title: Oozing Blood Filipino Pork Dinuguan
description: A classic Filipino dish made with pork blood, pork belly, and spices, served in a lacquerware bowl. Perfect for a weekend brunch.
instructions: Combine pork belly and pork blood in a large pot and cook over medium heat until the blood has thickened and the mixture is hot.
Add onions, garlic, bay leaves, black pepper, vinegar, patis, and salt to the pot and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add chili peppers, if using, and simmer for an additional 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Simmer the dinuguan for an additional 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
Serve the dinuguan hot in a lacquerware bowl and garnish with chopped onions and chili peppers, if desired.
Reheat leftovers over low heat, stirring occasionally, until hot and bubbly.
Serve leftovers with steamed rice or with eggs, for a filling breakfast.
This dinuguan recipe is a classic Filipino dish that is sure to become a favorite.
It's also a great way to use up leftover pork blood and belly.
Serve it for a special occasion or as a comfort food.
This dish is best served fresh, as it will thicken significantly as it cools.
